chapter: Swing and what makes a band play
title: Dizzy's groups and drummers who could not swing the big band
summary: He says Dizzy's groups did not swing like his sessions with Bird, citing Mickey Roker unable to swing a big band in Europe, and swinging is subjective.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, that's a very interesting subject. There's something I want to ask you both, to go back

to Diz a minute. I mean, you know how hot and bothered he got everybody and all the young trumpet players and all the different players? You know, who just felt that what he was doing was just the last word, you know? Well, the groups that he was playing with -- I mean, would you say, in a way, that none of it was really swinging? You know what I mean?

I know it didn't swing. Here's one of the reasons I said they didn't swing. Now look, there was more swinging when he and Bird did something than any other group you ever heard Dizz with. There's Mickey Rok6 -- that's Dizz's number one drummer. When we went over to Europe and did that thing with George Wein with the big band? Mickey couldn't swing that big band. He couldn't swing that big band, you know what I mean?

And it left me cold because he wasn't swinging, see? See, in other words, swing. I didn't want no -- a whole lot of technical stuff being done, because when you get technical, you can't swing. When you get technical, you got too much happening in there.
Jay, did you ever hear Kenny Clarke?
Does he swing for your money?
Well, I never heard him play that much, I'll tell you the truth, really. I never heard him play that
Didn't hear him play with a band or anything?
Well, swinging is a peculiar thing when you come down to it.
I mean, one person thinks a thing is swinging and another doesn't.
So now there's a subjective element there that you can't really pin down.
